match.reason: The bank point covers the same idea at the same depth: most water is salt water in the oceans, much fresh water is frozen or underground, and rivers and lakes hold only a tiny share.

confirm.reason: The closest bank point, Forms of water, covers where water is stored. It also teaches that water exists as liquid, ice and vapour and that each form can become a resource, so it is broader than this point, which is only about where Earth's water is held.

draft.title: Where the Earth's water is stored
card: Almost all of the Earth's water is salty, and most of it is in the oceans. Only a small share is fresh water.
Most fresh water is not easy to use. A large part is locked up as ice in glaciers and ice sheets.
Much of the rest is held underground in aquifers, which are layers of rock or sand that hold water in their gaps.
Only a tiny share of fresh water is in rivers and lakes, yet people use these stores a great deal.
draft.remember: Most water is salty ocean. Most fresh water is ice or underground. Rivers and lakes hold very little.

a.q: Which store holds the largest amount of the Earth's water?
a.why: Almost all of the Earth's water is salty and in the oceans. Ice holds most of the fresh water, but that is only a small share of all water, so it cannot be the largest store.
a.clue: Think of all water, not only fresh water.

b.q: Priya says rivers and lakes must hold most of the Earth's fresh water because people see and use them so often. What is wrong with her idea?
opts: Most fresh water is in ice or underground
Most fresh water is stored in the oceans
Rivers and lakes hold salty water only
Most fresh water is in the air as vapour
b.why: People use rivers and lakes a lot, but they hold only a tiny share of fresh water. Most fresh water is locked in ice or held in aquifers. Being easy to see does not mean a store is large.
b.clue: Seeing a store often does not tell you how big it is.

b.best: Most fresh water is in ice or underground
